key_insight: PyroDash makes LLM-grade reasoning cheaper by letting a small language model decide, token by token, when to call a larger model for help. This preserves high-quality answers on hard parts while avoiding unnecessary large-model usage on easy tokens.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the high cost and inefficiency of serving large language models for every generation step, especially when many tokens could be handled by a smaller, cheaper model. It aims to improve reliability on difficult reasoning tasks without paying full LLM inference cost throughout.
method: A small language model generates tokens and emits a special control token when it needs assistance.
A Collaborate Engine sends the current query plus the partial reasoning trace to a frozen large language model.
The large model completes the hard part of generation, enabling token-level collaboration instead of all-or-nothing switching.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a practical path to reduce inference cost while keeping strong reasoning performance. It is especially relevant for production systems that need to balance latency, accuracy, and serving budget.
